text:
cheng: heads up — after the merge from PR 8421 we're seeing a compile storm on the small-batch path. compile_rate spiked ~3x and kernel-autopick is oscillating between int8_fast and fp16_vec for the same model instances.

sam: ack, timeline? did CI show anything before merge? :eyes:

cheng: merge landed at 09:12am UTC. CI perf was green but I see the warm-run benchmark on staging fail at 09:18 with 99th latency jumps and many compilations started. logs attached in thread.

lauren: can you paste the selector debug dump? I want to see scores and why autotune flips.

cheng: paste below (trimmed):

```
selector: model=redwood-13b, seq=128
candidates: [int8_fast (score=0.51), fp16_vec (score=0.50), int8_safe (score=0.49)]
autotune.threshold=0.02
decision: pick=int8_fast
then next request: int8_fast score drops to 0.46, fp16_vec=0.47 -> switch
```

maria: that threshold is tiny — tiny score deltas + sampling noise will flip picks under short sequences. sounds like the autotune calibration change from PR 8421 adjusted the normalization.

sam: we should bisect to the exact commit in 8421 that modified selector normalization. cheng, can you run a quick bisect on staging? script: `./scripts/bisect-selector --range=8421~10..8421`

cheng: running now. running two-point comparison on staging canary. if reproduce, will collect KV cache metrics — I suspect cache churn because compiles evict artifacts which causes cascaded compiles.

deploy-bot: rollout blocked: automatic canary abort triggered (compile storm > 200 compiles / min). Action required by eng-runtime team.

lauren: perf profile from the warm-run attached: heap of compile tasks aligning with selector flips. also seeing kvcache evictions spike at the same time. I think the new normalization reduces score margins for longer sequences causing tie flips on short ones which then trigger new kernel compiles due to variant mismatch.

maria: proposed immediate mitigation: raise autotune.threshold to 0.05 for the affected models and enable sticky-pick for 10s to avoid rapid flips. I'll open a fast patch and a revert PR if bisect confirms.

sam: +1. also add a short cooldown after a compile for that model-instance so we avoid back-to-back compiles. we can roll that as a config override for Dedicated pools.

cheng: bisect result: culprit commit 8421+3 changed normalization from L2 to L1 (intended to stabilise extreme scores) but for our score distribution it reduced dynamic range. reproduces locally with `./bench/repro --seed=42 --shortseq`.

maria: thanks. PR 8421+3 revert created: #8439 (hotfix). pushing to canary now, will monitor compile rate.

oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-139: "compile storm due to autotune normalization change" assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

cheng: after rolling revert to canary, compile rate dropped to baseline and kvcache evictions returned to normal. rolling to prod after 10m stable.

maria: follow-ups: add unit tests for selector score distribution, add a perf regression checkpoint in CI for compile counts, and add sticky-pick cooldown config. documented in the rollback PR. :thumbsup:
